cards.back:
Title: El Castillo (Pyramid of Kukulcán)
Artist: Unknown (Maya builders)
Period/Culture: Maya (Terminal Classic, Maya-Toltec)
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 800-900 CE · Location: Chichén Itzá, Yucatán, Mexico
• Medium: Limestone masonry; stepped pyramid with four stairways and a temple on top
• Subject: Temple-pyramid to Kukulcán, the feathered serpent god
• Patron: Unknown; Chichén Itzá's ruling elite
• Meaning: A stone calendar: 91 steps x 4 sides + top platform = 365; at the equinoxes, shadows form a serpent sliding down the north stair
• Terms: None listed for this unit
(Look for, not scored: Architecture; feathered-serpent heads carved at the base of the north stair. Pose: N/A (architecture).)

Title: Purse cover from the Sutton Hoo ship burial
Artist: Unknown
Period/Culture: Early Medieval / Anglo-Saxon
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 625 CE · Location: Suffolk, England; now British Museum
• Medium: Gold, garnet, and glass cloisonné
• Subject: A man standing between two beasts; eagles attacking ducks; animal interlace
• Patron: Made for the royal burial, likely King Rædwald of East Anglia
• Meaning: Royal status and warrior-king wealth; the treasure burial parallels Beowulf
• Terms: cloisonné, zoomorphic, Beowulf, Middle Ages/medieval
(Look for, not scored: Flat, abstract, symmetrical, zoomorphic interlace. Pose: Frontal man flanked symmetrically by two beasts.)

Title: Chi-Rho-Iota (XPI) page, Book of Kells
Artist: Unknown monks
Period/Culture: Early Medieval / Hiberno-Saxon
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 800 CE · Location: Probably Iona, Scotland, then Kells, Ireland; now Trinity College Dublin
• Medium: Tempera (pigment) on vellum; hand-illuminated manuscript made in a scriptorium
• Subject: XPI, the first Greek letters of Christ's name, opening Matthew 1:18 (Christ's birth)
• Patron: Columban monks (Iona, then Kells); no single named patron
• Meaning: Glorifies the word of God and Christ's incarnation; making the book was an act of devotion
• Terms: scriptorium, zoomorphic, tempera, Middle Ages/medieval
(Look for, not scored: Dense interlace, spirals, tiny zoomorphic details (cats and mice, an otter with a fish), angels. Pose: N/A (page design).)

cards.back:
Title: Virgin and Child (Morgan Madonna)
Artist: Unknown
Period/Culture: Romanesque (Auvergne, France)
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 1150-1200 · Location: Auvergne, France; now Metropolitan Museum of Art, NY
• Medium: Painted wood (walnut), carved
• Subject: Mary seated with the Christ Child on her lap
• Patron: Unknown
• Meaning: A Throne of Wisdom: Mary is the throne, Christ is divine wisdom; carried in processions
• Terms: Throne of Wisdom, Romanesque
(Look for, not scored: Stiff, frontal, symmetrical; stylized, rigid drapery folds. Pose: Mary seated frontally, Christ upright on her lap facing forward.)

cards.front: Identify: title, artist, period/culture, and the battle and year it shows
cards.back:
Title: Bayeux Tapestry
Artist: Unknown (probably English embroiderers)
Period/Culture: Romanesque (Norman)
Event: Battle of Hastings, 1066
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 1070-1080 · Location: Probably made in England; kept in Bayeux, France
• Medium: Embroidered wool on linen, about 230 ft long; technically embroidery, not tapestry
• Subject: The Norman Conquest of England and the Battle of Hastings (1066); includes Halley's Comet
• Patron: Probably Bishop Odo of Bayeux, William the Conqueror's half-brother
• Meaning: Norman justification of the conquest, told as continuous visual history
• Terms: embroidery, Romanesque
(Look for, not scored: Flat, simplified figures in a continuous narrative strip; animal borders. Pose: Active, narrative poses: riding, fighting, falling.)

Title: Abbey church of Saint-Denis (choir)
Artist: Unknown builders
Period/Culture: Early Gothic, French
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 1140-1144 (choir) · Location: Saint-Denis, near Paris, France
• Medium: Stone; ambulatory choir with rib vaults, pointed arches, and large stained-glass windows
• Subject: Burial church of French kings, dedicated to Saint Denis
• Patron: Abbot Suger
• Meaning: First Gothic building: thin walls opened to colored light, lux nova, meant to lift the soul to God
• Terms: Abbot Suger, pointed arch, rib vault, stained glass, lux nova, pilgrimage
(Look for, not scored: N/A (architecture). Pose: N/A (architecture).)

Title: Virgin of Jeanne d'Évreux
Artist: Unknown Parisian goldsmiths
Period/Culture: Late Gothic, French
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: 1324-1339 · Location: Paris; given to Saint-Denis; now the Louvre
• Medium: Silver gilt with basse-taille enamel, gold, crystal, pearls
• Subject: Virgin and Child
• Patron: Queen Jeanne d'Évreux, who gave it to Saint-Denis in 1339
• Meaning: Luxury art and a reliquary: the fleur-de-lis held relics of Mary
• Terms: luxury art, reliquary, fleur-de-lis
(Look for, not scored: Elegant, courtly, slender. Pose: S-curve sway; the Child reaches playfully toward Mary's face.)
cards.commons: Virgin and Child Jeanne d'Evreux Louvre

cards.back:
Title: Röttgen Pietà
Artist: Unknown
Period/Culture: Late Gothic, German
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 1300-1325 · Location: Rhineland, Germany; now Rheinisches Landesmuseum, Bonn
• Medium: Painted wood, carved
• Subject: Mary mourning the dead Christ across her lap
• Patron: Unknown
• Meaning: A private devotional image (Andachtsbild) meant to make the viewer share Mary's grief
• Terms: Pietà
(Look for, not scored: Expressive and grotesque: emaciated Christ, large grape-like wounds. Pose: Mary holds Christ's rigid body stiffly across her lap.)

Title: Gates of Paradise (east doors, Baptistery)
Artist: Lorenzo Ghiberti
Period/Culture: Early Italian Renaissance
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: 1425-1452 · Location: Baptistery of San Giovanni, Florence
• Medium: Gilded bronze relief, cast
• Subject: Ten Old Testament scenes
• Patron: The Arte di Calimala (Florence's cloth merchants' guild)
• Meaning: Shows linear perspective in relief; Michelangelo reportedly named them; Ghiberti's self-portrait is in the frame
• Terms: linear perspective, atmospheric perspective, Humanism
(Look for, not scored: Classical, naturalistic figures. Pose: Varied, natural poses in deep architectural settings.)
cards.commons: Ghiberti Gates of Paradise Florence Baptistery doors

cards.back:
Title: David
Artist: Donatello
Period/Culture: Early Italian Renaissance
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 1440-1460 · Location: Medici palace courtyard, Florence; now the Bargello
• Medium: Bronze, cast
• Subject: Young David standing on Goliath's severed head after the fight
• Patron: The Medici family (likely Cosimo de' Medici)
• Meaning: First freestanding life-size nude since antiquity; Florence beating stronger enemies
• Terms: Medici family, Humanism
(Look for, not scored: Classical nude, youthful, idealized. Pose: Contrapposto, relaxed; hand on hip, shepherd's hat.)

Title: Primavera
Artist: Sandro Botticelli
Period/Culture: Early Italian Renaissance
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 1482 · Location: Florence (Medici commission); now the Uffizi
• Medium: Tempera on wood panel
• Subject: Venus in an orange grove with Cupid, the Three Graces, Mercury, Flora, and Zephyrus chasing Chloris
• Patron: The Medici (Lorenzo di Pierfrancesco de' Medici)
• Meaning: Humanist, Neoplatonic allegory of love and spring
• Terms: tempera, Medici family, Humanism
(Look for, not scored: Elongated, graceful, linear figures. Pose: Venus central and calm; figures read right to left.)

Title: Last Supper
Artist: Leonardo da Vinci
Period/Culture: High Renaissance
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: ca. 1495-1498 · Location: Refectory, Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan
• Medium: Oil and tempera on dry plaster (a secco); flaked within decades
• Subject: The moment after Christ says one of the apostles will betray him
• Patron: Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan (for the Santa Maria delle Grazie refectory)
• Meaning: Christ's head is the vanishing point; psychological drama of betrayal
• Terms: a secco, linear perspective, chiaroscuro, oil paint
(Look for, not scored: Naturalistic, emotional reactions. Pose: Christ calm and triangular at the center; apostles in four groups of three.)

cards.back:
Title: David
Artist: Michelangelo Buonarroti
Period/Culture: High Renaissance
Date: 1501-1504 (the one date you must know)
Also good to know (not scored):
• Date: 1501-1504 · Location: Florence; now Galleria dell'Accademia
• Medium: Marble, carved from an abandoned block (about 17 ft)
• Subject: David before the fight with Goliath
• Patron: Florence Cathedral works (Opera del Duomo), for the Florentine Republic
• Meaning: Civic symbol of the Florentine Republic standing against tyranny
• Terms: Humanism
(Look for, not scored: Idealized, heroic nude; oversized head and hands. Pose: Contrapposto, tense and alert, looking toward the enemy.)
